stem: Which child most closely matches the peak epidemiology of paediatric oro-facial trauma?
explanation: A 3-year-old boy best matches the peak epidemiology of paediatric oro-facial trauma, which is most common at 2 to 4 years of age and occurs more often in boys.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Correct because a 3-year-old boy fits the peak age range of 2 to 4 years and the male predominance described.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because 8 years is beyond the peak 2 to 4 year age range, and girls are less commonly affected than boys.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because 12 years is well beyond the peak 2 to 4 year age range.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because 6 months is younger than the peak age range, even though the sex does not change the age mismatch.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because 15 years is well beyond the peak 2 to 4 year age range, despite male sex fitting the reported predominance.
